To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
flash memory errors are cycle-, location-, and value-dependent.

(1) the errors that are most likely to occur are the ones that are most likely not to be detected by error correction codes; (2) errors are more likely to occur in the middle of a page than near its boundaries; (3) errors occur more frequently after the first write than after subsequent writes; (4) errors are more frequent in the first half of a page than in the second half; (5) errors in a page are correlated to errors in adjacent pages.
flash memory errors exhibit cycle-dependency, value-dependency, and location-dependency, which are caused by the underlying circuit and device characteristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the nature of flash memory errors and how to design algorithms to mitigate them.
understanding flash errors and the impact of flash errors on the performance and lifetime of flash-based storage devices.
the characterization of error patterns and their causes in flash memory.

the error patterns discovered are not random.

the flash memory industry is moving from a technology-centric to an algorithm-centric approach, and that our work is an important step towards this goal.

flash error patterns are highly complex and depend on the type of operation, the location of the operation and the number of cycles.
